§10.4.2 Checkboxes

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

forms-checkboxes · forms

✅ Normative

A checked box MUST be rendered as [x] and an unchecked box as [ ]. An unchecked box MUST be transcribed explicitly and MUST NOT be dropped.

What counts as checked

A box is checked when it holds a clear, unambiguous mark inside it — a check, a cross, a filled box.

  • Handwriting or a mark near a box MUST NOT make it checked.
  • A box whose state is in doubt MUST be rendered [ ].
  • A decorative bullet (●) printed beside a required field is not a check mark.

The rendered page decides

A check mark can exist only as drawn strokes with no text-layer glyph — common on degraded scans. The state MUST be read from the rendered page, never from the text layer: a tick the text layer never saw is still a tick. See The Page Is the Ground Truth§2.1.

A lone labelled checkbox

The box sits in the value position:

- **FATCA filing requirement**: [x]
- \[D\] **Check if this is a publicly traded partnership (PTP)**: [ ]

A checkbox with its own write-in

One line — the box first, then the entered text:

- \[3\] [x] 8888
- **Other (specify):** [x] consulting

Every box on the page

A checkbox MUST be included wherever it sits — header, margin, footer: Final K-1 / Amended K-1 at the very top of a K-1, CORRECTED (if checked) at the top of a 1099. See Fields Outside the Form§10.5.1.

Radio buttons

A radio control MUST be rendered with the same [ ] / [x] notation as a checkbox. Every option MUST be kept, with its grouping, and a printed pick-one instruction MUST be kept as text.

✅ Sample — radio buttons beside checkboxes

A motion form with [ ☐ ] bracketed boxes for the reasons and [ ○ ] bracketed circles for DENIED / GRANTED and objects / does not object. The circles are pick-one controls; the notation is [ ] or [x], preserving each printed state. A Print Form button sits at the foot.
